thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for inference-queue (P1) - high queue backlog + autoscaler falling behind. Alert: inference-queue.length > 4000 for 2m; autoscaler_events.rate_of_scale_down_retries > 0. Link: https://pagerduty.internal/pd/INC-4871

pagerduty: Page fired -> INC-4871. Assigned to on-call rotation: maya. Escalation policy: 3m -> oliver (secondary).

maya: ack. I'm on it. grabbing metrics now.

oliver: ack. ping if you need handoff. heard from monitoring that tail latencies are spiking to 12s and some 429s.

maya: quick snapshot: prometheus shows continuous enqueue > 7k/min, processing throughput ~3.5k/min. autoscaler hasn't added nodes in last 8m. HPA visible, but node pool quota at 100%.

sasha: how confident are we this is quota vs kube API throttle? we just had cloud provider spot reclaim in us-east-1 earlier.

maya: logs show lots of "scale_out_request denied: quota_exceeded" from cloud-provisioner. K8s events show failed pod scheduling: InsufficientGPU.

devon: ok that matches infra alert about hitting GPU pool cap. I'm going to request temporary burst quota. pinging cloud-ops.

devon: (private) /me submitted emergency quota request + manual spinup ticket to cloud-ops (#cloud-ops). ETA ~7-10m if approved.

oliver: we should mitigate customer impact first — can we drain slow model variants or route non-critical traffic to cpu-fallback?

maya: yes. plan: 1) enable model fallback routing for non-enterprise customers 2) pause low-priority demo routes 3) manual scale for critical workers if nodes freed or via reserved instances. I'll apply routing change now.

maya: @ops-bot run: 
```
# switch routing rule: route -> cpu-variant for tag:free-tier
redwoodctl routing set --route "api.v1.generate" --rule "if customer.tier==free then model=cpu-small"
```

ops-bot: routing change queued. Applying... done. :white_check_mark: Traffic shift ~18% away from GPU variants.

sasha: good. can we also reduce batch sizes temporarily to lower per-request mem pressure? that'll increase token compute but may let more pods stay healthy.

maya: patching serving config for inference-worker: set batch.max_tokens=512 -> 256 and batch.max_requests=16 -> 8.

maya: config change applied. watchers: please confirm latency impact.

oliver: saw immediate reduction in OOMs on new pods attempts. latency increased a hair for long sequences but overall throughput looks steadier.

devon: cloud-ops responded: temporary burst quota approved, provisioning 4 additional GPU instances now. ETA ~4m to kube nodes ready.

maya: great. I'm going to manually scale deployment replicas to make pods schedule quicker once nodes are ready: 
```
kubectl scale deploy inference-worker -n redwood-prod --replicas=20
```

maya: command run. will watch pod scheduling.

oliver: seeing pod Pending -> ContainerCreating -> CrashLoopBackOff for a few due to KV cache cold startup causing OOMs. we should throttle rollout to avoid repeated evictions.

maya: rolling update strategy -> set maxUnavailable=10%. patching.
```
kubectl patch deployment inference-worker -n redwood-prod -p '{"spec": {"strategy": {"rollingUpdate": {"maxUnavailable": "10%"}}}}'
```

ops-bot: patch applied.

sasha: also enable prefix KV warmup for the busiest models to reduce initial cold token surge. can do small warmup batch of top 50 prefixes.

maya: scheduling warmup jobs now: 
```
redwoodctl jobs create --name kv-warmup-top50 --model gpt-infer-v3 --prefixes-file /tmp/top50.txt
```

maya: warmup jobs scheduled.

pagerduty: INC-4871 acknowledged by maya at 4912345682. Next escalation suppressed.

oliver: tracking customer impact: internal SLO dashboard shows error rate on customer-facing endpoints up from 0.2% -> 3.8% (mainly 429s + timeouts). Enterprise customers with reserved capacity unaffected so far, but a handful of high-QPS tenants on shared pool saw degraded throughput. noted.

devon: cloud nodes becoming Ready. 3/4 new GPU nodes joined cluster at 4912345980. one still provisioning.

maya: pods starting to schedule. backlog length trending down: 7.1k -> 3.9k in last 6m. throughput improved to ~5.8k/min.

sasha: nice. monitor KV warmup logs for progress. some prefixes have high cache miss during the first 30s.

maya: KV warmup showing ~60% of targets warmed after first batch. second batch queued.

oliver: runbook check: if autoscaler still fails after nodes available, we should rotate to reserved pool and adjust autoscaler thresholds: set scale up threshold to 65% CPU/GPU utilization to trigger earlier.

maya: agreed. I'll open a config PR after we stabilize.

devon: last node joined at 4912346060. cluster capacity restored. autoscaler caught up and resumed normal activity.

ops-bot: backlog drain progress: 3.9k -> 1.2k at 4912346200.

maya: customer impact update: error rate falling back toward baseline. still monitoring 429s for a small set of routes. reaching out to CS to flag impacted tenants and offer mitigation.

oliver: re: PagerDuty - INC-4871, recommend close after 1h of stable metrics and backlog <500.

sasha: will follow up with a short post-incident note: root cause = GPU pool quota + autoscaler tie-breaker bug that prevented scale-out when provisioning failures occurred. follow-ups: auto-burst path, autoscaler retry logic fix, and better alerting on quota rejections.

maya: agreed. setting incident status -> monitoring. I'll hand off to oliver for long-form postmortem.

oliver: taking postmortem lead. assigning action items.

maya: closing loop on PD: clearing ack and resolving page. pagerduty: resolving INC-4871 at 4912346265.

pagerduty: INC-4871 resolved by maya.

devon: adding notes to ticket and cloud-ops thread with timestamps and quota approval details.

sasha: :white_check_mark: Good job team. I'll draft a tl;dr and action list in #incidents.

maya: thanks all. I'll follow up with perf graphs and rollout plan for autoscaler fix.

ops-bot: summary metrics snapshot attached (link: https://metrics.internal/snapshot/INC-4871).

maya: thread lock for now, but keep monitoring for 30m.

oliver: copying into oncall rotation notes for tomorrow.

incident-bot: Note: incident closed, record created: INC-4871.
